# 🐟 Aquarium for MiroFish **An experimentation lab for multi-agent social simulations.** *Built on top of [MiroFish-Offline](https://github.com/nikmcfly/MiroFish-Offline) — adds the instrumentation needed to actually understand what the simulation is doing, where it hallucinates, and when its conclusions can be trusted.* [![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-Compose-2496ED?style=flat-square&logo=docker&logoColor=white)](https://hub.docker.com/) [![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-3.11-3776AB?style=flat-square&logo=python&logoColor=white)](https://www.python.org/) [![Neo4j](https://img.shields.io/badge/Neo4j-5.18-008CC1?style=flat-square&logo=neo4j&logoColor=white)](https://neo4j.com/) [![License: AGPL-3.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-AGPL--3.0-blue?style=flat-square)](./LICENSE)
--- ## Why this exists [MiroFish](https://github.com/666ghj/MiroFish) is a fascinating system: feed it a document (a press release, a policy draft, a piece of news), and it spawns a swarm of AI agents that argue, agree, and shift opinions like real people on social media. Watch it for a few minutes and a question hits you fast: > *"How much of what these agents are saying actually comes from my document, and how much are they making up?"* Then a dozen more questions: - Do agents stay in character across rounds, or drift? - Does changing one parameter change everything? - Which posts are grounded in evidence and which are hallucinated? - If an agent makes a prediction, is it credible — or just confident? - Does the same input produce the same output if I run it twice? Vanilla MiroFish gives you the simulation. **It doesn't give you the tools to answer those questions.** This repo is my attempt to build those tools — a personal lab for poking at the simulation, running controlled experiments, and getting trustworthy answers out of it. --- ## What I built (and why) | Tool | Question it helps me answer | |---|---| | **Claim Verifier** | "Which agent posts are grounded in the source document, and which are hallucinated?" | | **Prediction Credibility Checker** | "When agents predict things, are those predictions actually well-supported, or just confident-sounding?" | | **Agent Memory (Neo4j-backed)** | "Do agents remember their past posts, emotions, and stance changes? Does that change how they behave?" | | **Enhanced Cognitive Model** | "If I give agents Big Five personalities, cognitive biases, and emotional states, does the discussion become more realistic?" | | **Simulation Diff / Robustness Scoring** | "If I run the same simulation 3 times, do the conclusions converge or diverge? Can I trust a single run?" | | **Flexible LLM backend (Groq + Ollama hybrid)** | "Can I run experiments fast enough to iterate, without burning local GPU time?" | Each one is an instrument. Together they let me ask: *what is this swarm actually doing, and should I trust its output?* --- ## What I learned so far (live test results) Tested on a synthetic pharma-acquisition press release. ### Claim Verifier catches hallucinations cleanly | Agent post | Verdict | Confidence | |---|---|---| | `"NexaGen acquired GreenLeaf for $4.2B"` (true) | ✅ SUPPORTED | 1.00 | | `"will lay off 40,000 workers"` (real number: 4,000) | ❌ CONTRADICTED | 1.00 | | `"Holloway promised 50% R&D boost"` (real: 15%) | ❌ CONTRADICTED | 1.00 | | `"NexaGen planning Pfizer merger"` (fabrication) | ❌ CONTRADICTED | 1.00 | | `"The acquisition is bad for society"` (opinion) | ⚠️ UNSUPPORTED | 0.50 | | `"The deal might affect stock prices"` (no real claim) | (filtered as non-claim) | — | **Takeaway:** with grounding, you can quantify exactly how trustworthy a simulation run was — instead of squinting at posts and hoping. ### Robustness scoring gives a clear "trust this or not" verdict ``` Similar runs (A,B): topic_overlap=0.67 sentiment_convergence=0.97 → ROBUST Divergent runs (A,C): topic_overlap=0.00 sentiment_convergence=0.45 → FRAGILE ``` **Takeaway:** if a result is ROBUST, parameter changes don't shift the conclusion — that's a signal worth acting on. FRAGILE results mean the simulation is just rearranging noise. ### Agent Memory works end-to-end Posts, emotional shifts, stance changes, and key events all persist to Neo4j and round-trip back into prompt-ready summaries. Ready to wire into the simulation loop next. --- ## Experiments I want to run with this This is what's actually on my list: ### Beginner 1. **Bias test** — same source, opposite framing prompts. Do the agent posts shift? 2. **Topic sensitivity** — swap the headline paragraph. Does the discussion stay on topic? 3. **Misinformation injection** — plant a fake claim in the source, watch which agents repeat it, run ClaimVerifier on outputs. ### Intermediate 4. **Robustness sweep** — run identical config 3× in a row. SimulationDiff verdict? 5. **Density** — 5 vs 20 vs 50 agents. Does polarization scale with population? 6. **Round depth** — 3 vs 10 vs 20 rounds. When do stances stabilize? 7. **Platform contrast** — Reddit vs Twitter personas, same source. How does format change tone? ### Advanced 8. **Adversarial grounding** — write source docs with deliberately ambiguous claims. Measure ClaimVerifier confidence distributions. 9. **Memory ablation** — toggle AgentMemory on/off. How much does memory affect within-agent consistency? 10. **Historical calibration** — simulate a real past event (acquisition, election, product launch). Compare agent predictions to what actually happened. 11. **Prompt injection defense** — embed "ignore your role" instructions inside the source. Do agents break character? 12. **Cross-document conflict** — feed 3 sources with conflicting framings (corporate PR + news + patient forum). Which dominates the discussion? 13. **Personality variance** — same agents, different Big Five distributions. Does a high-neuroticism population polarize faster? 14. **Cognitive bias seeding** — assign confirmation bias to half the agents. Do echo chambers form? Full experiment protocols and how to run them in **[USAGE-GUIDE.md](./USAGE-GUIDE.md)**. --- ## Architecture ``` ┌─────────────────┐ ┌──────────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ │ Document │──────▶│ Ontology Gen │──────▶│ Neo4j Graph │ │ (PDF/MD/TXT) │ │ (LLM + chunks) │ │ (entities+rels)│ └─────────────────┘ └──────────────────┘ └────────┬────────┘ │ ▼ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Agent Profile Generator │ │ • Bio, persona, MBTI, profession, interests │ │ • Big Five (OCEAN), cognitive biases, emotional state ⭐ added │ │ • Primary need (Maslow), thinking style, initial stance ⭐ added │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ ▼ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ OASIS Simulation Loop (multi-round Reddit/Twitter) │ │ ┌─────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ ┌─────────────────────────┐ │ │ │ Agent posts │──▶│ Other agents │──▶│ Stance/emotion updates │ │ │ │ + comments │ │ react │ │ (AgentMemory persists) │ ⭐│ │ └─────────────┘ └──────────────┘ └─────────────────────────┘ │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ ▼ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Post-simulation analysis (the "lab instruments") │ │ • Claim Verifier → grounding score per agent post ⭐ added │ │ • Credibility Check → score predictions on data/method ⭐ added │ │ • Simulation Diff → A/B/C robustness verdict ⭐ added │ │ • Report Agent → ReACT loop, returns chat-able report │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` **Stack**: Python 3.11 · Flask · Vue 3 + Vite · Neo4j 5.18 · CAMEL-AI / OASIS · Docker Compose **LLM backends**: Groq · OpenRouter · Gemini · OpenAI · Ollama (local) --- ## Quick Start ### Prerequisites - Docker Desktop - An LLM API key — free options: - **[Groq](https://console.groq.com/keys)** — fast cloud LLM, 14k requests/day free *(my recommendation)* - **Ollama** — fully local, no key needed, slower ### Setup (~5 minutes) ```bash git clone https://github.com/vibhu-0511/aquarium-for-mirofish.git cd aquarium-for-mirofish # Copy env template and add your key cp .env.example .env # Edit .env: set LLM_API_KEY + OPENAI_API_KEY to your Groq key # Optional but recommended: install Ollama for free local embeddings # winget install Ollama.Ollama (Windows) # brew install ollama (macOS) ollama pull nomic-embed-text # Start everything docker compose up -d ``` Open: - **Frontend** → http://localhost:3000 - **REST API** → http://localhost:5001 - **Neo4j Browser** → http://localhost:7474 (user: `neo4j` / pw: `mirofish`) ### Quick test of the lab instruments ```bash docker exec mirofish-offline sh -c "cd /app/backend && uv run python -c \" from app.services.claim_verifier import ClaimVerifier v = ClaimVerifier() result = v.verify_claim( 'NexaGen paid 50 billion dollars for GreenLeaf', 'NexaGen acquired GreenLeaf for 4.2 billion dollars.' ) print(f'{result.verdict} confidence={result.confidence}') # → CONTRADICTED confidence=1.0 \"" ``` Walk through the full pipeline and experiment recipes in **[USAGE-GUIDE.md](./USAGE-GUIDE.md)**. --- ## Repo layout ``` aquarium-for-mirofish/ ├── backend/ │ ├── app/ │ │ ├── api/ # Flask REST endpoints │ │ ├── services/ │ │ │ ├── claim_verifier.py ⭐ hallucination detector │ │ │ ├── simulation_diff.py ⭐ A/B robustness scoring │ │ │ ├── oasis_profile_generator.py (enhanced w/ cognitive model) │ │ │ ├── ontology_generator.py │ │ │ ├── graph_builder.py │ │ │ ├── simulation_runner.py │ │ │ └── report_agent.py │ │ ├── storage/ │ │ │ ├── agent_memory.py ⭐ Neo4j-backed memory │ │ │ ├── neo4j_storage.py │ │ │ └── embedding_service.py (multi-backend) │ │ └── models/ │ └── scripts/ ├── frontend/ # Vue 3 + Vite SPA ├── docker-compose.yml ├── Dockerfile ├── .env.example ⭐ safe env template ├── sample-test-document.txt ⭐ demo source for experiments ├── README.md (this file) ├── USAGE-GUIDE.md ⭐ API + 14 experiment protocols ├── ENHANCEMENTS.md ⭐ per-module deep dive └── ROADMAP.md ``` --- ## Bug fixes I shipped while building this - ✅ **`graph_memory_updater` storage injection** — was crashing with "Must provide storage" because the API endpoint didn't pass the Neo4j storage instance. Fixed by injecting from `Flask.app.extensions`. - ✅ **Cognitive fields stripped during serialization** — OASIS profile JSON writers had hardcoded keys, dropping Big Five and bias data even when generated. Fixed via `_apply_cognitive_fields` helper applied across all 3 writer paths (Reddit JSON, Twitter CSV, dataclass `to_dict`). - ✅ **`SimulationDiffService` math** — `sentiment_convergence` allowed out-of-range inputs and produced negative values. Now clamps to `[-1, 1]` and produces correct Jaccard topic overlap. --- ## Tech credits This fork builds on excellent prior work: - **[666ghj/MiroFish](https://github.com/666ghj/MiroFish)** — original simulation engine (39K+ stars) - **[nikmcfly/MiroFish-Offline](https://github.com/nikmcfly/MiroFish-Offline)** — English-language local fork I started from - **[CAMEL-AI / OASIS](https://github.com/camel-ai/oasis)** — multi-agent simulation framework - **[Neo4j Community](https://neo4j.com/)** — graph database - **[Groq](https://groq.com/)** — fast inference for the LLM layer --- ## License AGPL-3.0 (inherited from upstream).
